?Court No. - 1
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 2083 of 2023

Petitioner :- Balveer Singh
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, Lko. And Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- S.K. Singhaniya Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ramesh Sinha,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.
Shri S.K. Sighaniya, learned counsel for the petitioner and Shri Pavan Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A.
for the State/respondent Nos. 1 to 3 are present.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner - Balveer Singh with a prayer to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Certioari for quashing the impugned First Information Report dated 30.12.2022, registered as Case Crime No.0614/2022, under Sections 419, 420 IPC, at Police Station Mohanlalganj, District - Lucknow; with a further prayer to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the opposite party No.1 to 3 to not to arrest the petitioner in pursuance of the impugned F.I.R.
As per version of the F.I.R., the informant is working in the Indian Army.

The informant and his brother Rakesh Kumar had purchased a plot of land with the petitioner-accused and on 29.06.2022 Balveer Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48962887/

sentences.text: the petitioner-accused had given in writing that he would execute the sale deed but he neither gave land to the informant nor did he made any contact with the informant.
The accused has taken money from the informant but he is giving the land at some other place.
It has been argued by learned counsel for petitioner that petitioner has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence.
The F.I.R. has been lodged with malafide intention.
The sale-deed has been executed by the petitioner in favour of the informant and possession of the land has also been handed over to the informant.
Petitioner has not taken any illegal money from any person.
The allegations levelled against the petitioner are absolutely false, frivolous and baseless.
No offence is made out against the petitioner, hence, the impugned F.I.R. is liable to be quashed.
Learned A.G.A., on the other hand, opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel for petitioner and submitted that petitioner is named in the F.I.R.
Petitioner is a serial offender.
He is habitual of committing such crimes.

There are six cases lodged against the petitioner at different police stations of the District which are of the similar nature, to which learned counsel for the petitioner states that he has given explanation of four cases in para 9 of the writ petition.
In the present F.I.R. also the petitioner is actively involved.
Learned A.G.A. further submits that alleged offence is serious in nature as petitioner is involved in duping so many of investors.

He further submits that impugned F.I.R. discloses a cognizable offence against the petitioner and, therefore,
the present writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

Having examined the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusing the impugned F.I.R., which shows that cognizable offence is made out against the petitioner and also considering the criminal antecedents of the petitioner, we are of the opinion that no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the impugned F.I.R. or for grant of any interim relief to the petitioner.
The writ petition lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
It is needless to say that the petitioner is at liberty to take recourse to the remedy available under Section 438 Cr.P.C. or Section 439 Cr.P.C., as the case may be, if so desired.

(Narendra Kumar Johari,J.) (Ramesh Sinha,J.) Order Date :- 22.3.2023 ML/-
